ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ اللَّهُ (١)).
The words of the Exalted (هُوَ): there are two views on it. The first: it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and «اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the khabar of «هُوَ».
The second: it is a mubtadaʾ in the sense of "the one asked about", because they said: "Is your Lord of copper or of gold?" On this view «اللَّهُ» may be the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and «أَحَدٌ» a badal (substitute), or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. It is also possible for «اللَّهُ» to be a badal and «أَحَدٌ» the khabar. The hamza of «أَحَد» is substituted for a wāw, because it is in the sense of «الْوَاحِد» (the One); the substitution of hamza for a wāw bearing fatḥa is rare, and an instance of it is «امْرَأَةٌ أَنَاةٌ» (a deliberate, unhurried woman), i.e. «وَنَاةٌ», because it is from «الْوَنَى» (slackness).
It is also said that the hamza is original, like the hamza in «أَحَد» used for generality. Whoever drops the tanwīn (nunation) from «أَحَد» does so because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. [Translator's note: the verse is quoted in the source with «اللَّهُ» from the following verse (اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ) attached to it.]

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ (٤)).
The words of the Exalted (كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ): [«أَحَدٌ»] is the noun (ism) of «كَانَ». There are two views on its khabar (predicate):
The first: «كُفُوًا»; on this view «لَهُ» may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «كُفُوًا», because the implied form is «وَلَمْ يَكُنْ أَحَدٌ كُفُوًا لَهُ» (and none is equal to Him), or it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَكُنْ».
The second view: that the khabar is «لَهُ», and «كُفُوًا» is a ḥāl from «أَحَدٌ», i.e. «وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ أَحَدٌ كُفُوًا»; when the indefinite [adjective] was fronted, it was put in the accusative as a ḥāl. And Allah knows best.
